Both cut-outs stay coherent with no tearing, ghosting, doubled edges or awkward frame clipping, and the final near-full-frame view is a strong image to dwell on. The 1950s lithograph character is retained.

filmIssues: The pull-back is clearly visible and purposeful: it opens tight on the boy and red door, then steadily reveals the long, empty louvred corridor, expressing his exclusion and isolation. Both cut-outs remain coherent, with feet and door staying planted and no obvious tearing, doubled edges, or frame-edge clipping. The first frame is a strong close opening and the final wider frame is a good dwelling image. The dust is subtle and appropriate to the archive-print treatment.

s4.verdict: A clear, purposeful pull-back for loss. It opens tight on the man from behind, head in hands, then eases back to reveal the lamp-lit desk, rotary phone, tender files and the crane-filled window around him, leaving him smaller and isolated in the office. The subject stays coherent through the move with no visible tearing, doubled edges, halo or painted-over ghost, layers that belong together stay together, and no layer clips the frame awkwardly; both the tight first frame and the full final frame are strong still pictures to open and dwell on. The dust is subtle and the flat halftone silkscreen print character is preserved throughout.
s4.rationale: A loss after the bank's call: start tight on the man with his head in his hands and pull back, shrinking him slightly, to reveal the lamp-lit desk, phone, tender files and cranes of the unfinished city around him.

s6.verdict: Do not publish as-is: the concept fits the caption but the executed motion is too timid to clearly express the halving in value.
s6.rationale: Bolder pull-back for loss: start tight on the terrace row, board and lit toilet doorway, then pull back to the full plate while both houses and sign shrink to the minimum 0.85 scale and sink slightly, visibly diminished in the empty foreground. filmIssues: The pull-back idea is appropriate for loss/devaluation, but in the frames the change from t=0 to t=1 is very small and reads as a slow, timid zoom-out rather than a clear diminishment.
The houses and sign shrink too little to visibly express 'worth half'; the terrace row, board and toilet doorway remain at nearly the same visual weight throughout.
Both the opening and final frames are serviceable, but the final held frame retains the same centred composition as the opening, so the loss reveal does not land as a distinct final picture.
No obvious tearing, doubled edges, ghosting or awkward frame-edge clipping is visible, and the halftone-shimmer is subtle and era-appropriate.

s8.verdict: A purposeful pull-back for loss that is undermined by a visible ghost patch on the figure and an over-recession that leaves the final frame too empty.
s8.rationale: Bolder, story-first version of the same loss pull-back: start genuinely tight on the man-from-behind at zoom 1.45 focused on him, then pull back to the full empty boardroom at 1.0, while the locked cut-1/cut-2 figure itself walks away - drifting up the corridor (-0.055) and shrinking to 0.87 so he recedes toward the glass boardroom as the room is revealed empty around him. filmIssues: The pull-back / walk-away idea is clear and visible, but the man recedes twice over — camera zoom-out plus a -0.055 upward drift and 0.87 shrink — so by t=1 he is too small to hold the final, dwell-on frame.

A pale, toilet-shaped ghost patch appears on the man's back in the lower-row frames, indicating the identically-boxed cut-1/cut-2 layers are separating / showing through as they move. The figure does not stay fully coherent.
The t=0 frame at zoom 1.45 flattens the man against the table and chairs; his legs overlap the boardroom furniture and the entrance/walk-away reads confusingly before the pull-back clarifies it.
Halftone-shimmer is appropriate for the risograph print and is not distracting in the frames shown.

s12.verdict: A coherent, publishable-looking pull-back in stills, but the film is timid: the entrance close-up and floor-by-floor reveal the brief calls for never visibly happen, and there is no purposeful parallax.
s12.rationale: Bolder, undamped arrival-and-reveal: keep the maximum 1.5-to-1.0 pull-back but cut the large panY that was forcing the renderer to damp the whole move, and move the zoom focus down to the man/door (0.47, 0.84) so frame 0 is genuinely tight on the entrance in morning light. Pull back and rise steadily through office, kitchen and hall to the full Kampong Ubi centre at zoom 1.0 for the dwell. Both id
filmIssues: The intended 1.5-to-1.0 pull-back from the entrance is heavily muted in the contact sheet: all six frames already show the whole cutaway building, so frame 0 is not genuinely tight on the man and open door and the reveal of office, kitchen and hall barely registers.

There is almost no parallax or layer motion — the single listed layer has no drift, no scale change and depth 0.35, and cut-2 is absent from the plan — so the move reads as a plain, slow zoom-out rather than an arrival-and-reveal.
The light-sweep ambient is not legible in any frame; the morning light at the door does not strengthen or pass across the building.

First and last frames are both good, coherent pictures with no tearing, ghosting, doubled edges or awkward edge clipping, and the final full-building view is a strong dwell image — but the journey between them is too timid to express the scene's story.
